q: Why did CAC increase yesterday? Check whether the change came from CPM, CTR, CPC, landing-page conversion, checkout conversion, product mix, or channel mix. Rank the drivers by likely contribution.
answer:
Short answer — the premise was incorrect: CAC fell yesterday, it did not increase.

Key evidence (previous → 2026-10-13)
- CAC (Derived): ₹4,296 → ₹2,100.  
- Ad spend (Measured): ₹38,661 → ₹50,404 (+30.4%).  
- New customers (Measured): 9 → 24 (+166.7%).  
- CPM (Measured, shown rounded): ₹291 → ₹342 — change computed from those rounded figures: 17.5% (Derived from the shown values).  
- CTR (Derived): 2.6% → 2.9%.  
- CPC (Measured, shown rounded): ₹11.3 → ₹11.9 — change computed from those rounded figures: 5.3% (Derived from the shown values).  
- Landing-page views (Measured): 734 → 1,242 (+69.2%).  
- Checkout rate (Measured): 0.98% → 1.63% (+66.0%).  

Why (ranked likely contributors, labels)
1) New customer surge — largest contributor to the CAC decrease (Derived: customer rise more than offset higher spend).  
2) Ad spend increase — opposed the CAC improvement (Measured).  
3) Funnel uplift (landing-page → checkout → purchase) — positive driver of new customers (Measured → Hypothesis: explains conversion lift).  
4) Channel mix — Meta delivered most of the new-customer gain (Measured).  
5) Product mix — insufficient evidence to call it a driver (Hypothesis / insufficient evidence).
